headline: External sharing is immediate without review, though formal approval taking several days is recommended to remove the unapproved app warning.
summary: Atlassian provides a highly accessible OAuth 2.0 (3LO) setup for Jira. Developers can create an app, toggle it to 'Sharing', and allow arbitrary external users to connect immediately. End-users will see an 'unapproved app' warning banner until the developer submits the app for a formal, free review. API calls require an extra resource discovery step to route requests via the user's specific cloudId.
time_to_production: Immediate for unapproved sharing, 1 to 2 weeks for approved listing

oauth.pkce: Discovery metadata indicates S256 PKCE support, though documentation mandates a confidential client exchange.
oauth.refresh_tokens: Supported via offline_access scope. Tokens rotate on use with a 10-minute leeway and expire after 90 days of inactivity.
oauth.redirect_uri_rules: Strict exact match required. Must use HTTPS in production. http://localhost and http://127.0.0.1 are allowed for local dev.
oauth.scopes: Space-separated list. Atlassian recommends classic scopes (e.g., read:jira-work) and apps should stay below 50 total scopes.

steps.title: Register OAuth Application
steps.detail: Create a new OAuth 2.0 (3LO) integration in the Atlassian Developer Console.

steps.title: Configure Scopes and Redirects
steps.detail: Add Jira Cloud platform APIs, select classic read/write scopes, and set the callback URL.

steps.title: Toggle Sharing Setting
steps.detail: Navigate to the Distribution tab in the console and toggle the status to Sharing to allow external users to connect immediately.

steps.title: Submit for Warning Removal
steps.detail: Submit the app via the Marketplace portal as 'not directly installable', providing staging credentials and privacy URLs to remove the unapproved warning.

requirements.text: Integration must be submitted as 'My app isn't directly installable' when seeking approval.
Developer must provide working demo credentials, a staging account, or step-by-step external access instructions for reviewers.
App must provide public Privacy Policy and Terms of Service URLs.
App name and assets must not start with 'Jira' or use unmodified Atlassian logos.

gotchas.text: API requests require discovering the user's accessible cloudId first via the accessible-resources endpoint.
Refresh tokens are automatically rotated upon use; relying on a static refresh token will break the integration.
End-users will be presented with a prominent 'unapproved app' warning banner until the Atlassian review is completed.

permissions.review_impact: Does not require site admin consent for standard data access; user can consent directly.

blockers.issue: API returns HTTP 429 Too Many Requests due to rate limits
blockers.how_to_proceed: Implement exponential back-off and pause requests for the duration indicated by the Retry-After header in the response.

blockers.issue: Atlassian reviewer rejects app due to broken OAuth flow
blockers.how_to_proceed: Ensure you have provided a fully configured staging account with clear step-by-step instructions so the reviewer can complete end-to-end OAuth verification.

agent_can: Test token exchange endpoints and implement cloudId resource discovery
Draft privacy policy and terms of service documents for submission
Configure request headers and handle refresh token rotation logic
you_must: Register the developer account and create the app in the Atlassian Console
Toggle the distribution status to 'Sharing' to enable external access
Submit the application for formal review to remove the unapproved warning banner

key_claims.text: The Atlassian OAuth discovery metadata includes valid configuration and S256 PKCE support.
The authorization endpoint successfully blocks requests with invalid client IDs and redirect URIs.
Atlassian allows immediate external sharing of unapproved OAuth 3LO apps without any hard user quotas.
Formal review to remove the unapproved warning banner is free and typically takes days to a couple of weeks.

open_questions: Are there any undocumented burst rate limit caps specifically applied to unapproved applications?
